thesis: WTI settled 94.24 on 2026-09-08 (+3.0% d/d) and Brent traded near 99 intraday as renewed US-Iran fighting hit Saudi energy facilities and constrained Strait of Hormuz transits, and EIA STEO now expects Middle East shut-in production to persist into early 2027 rather than reversing this year. XLE closed 1.1% off its 200-day high with the 20-day (63.10), 50-day (59.42) and 200-day (54.93) stacked in order, so the pullback entry is into rising support rather than a reflex discount.
key_risk: This is a geopolitical premium, not a demand story. Iran said an Oman agreement on Hormuz shipping was nearing completion; a de-escalation headline unwinds the whole move overnight and XLE gaps through the stop, and OPEC+ is still restoring 2.2 mb/d of cut production into the same tape.
counter_argument: Buying an energy ETF within 1.1% of its 200-day high after crude has risen roughly 10% in a week is chasing a spike, and every prior Hormuz scare has round-tripped within weeks. The answer is the entry: the recommendation is explicitly to wait for 62.80-64.00, roughly 2.4% below the last print and at the 20-day, so a spike that round-trips is bought rather than chased, and the 60.70 stop sits below the 09-04 session low of 63.375 by more than a full ATR.

catalyst.event: QatarEnergy force majeure LNG cargo cancellations to European and Asian buyers now extended into early November 2026, with Ras Laffan still down ~12.8 Mtpa (~17% of Qatari capacity) after the March missile strikes — into the Northern Hemisphere heating season
catalyst.action: accumulate 266-276.5 while the stock consolidates under the 20-day; add on a close above 301

thesis: About 20% of the world's seaborne LNG passed through the Strait of Hormuz before the war, and Iranian strikes on Ras Laffan on 18-19 March took out two liquefaction trains plus a GTL unit — roughly 12.8 Mtpa, about 17% of Qatari capacity — with QatarEnergy force majeure cancellations to Europe and Asia now running into early November. That makes US Gulf liquefaction the marginal global supplier into winter, and Cheniere is the largest US exporter, running Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi with EIA putting full-year US export volumes near 17.0 Bcf/d.
key_risk: Cheniere is a tolling business: the great majority of its volumes are sold under fixed-fee long-term SPAs, so a higher JKM/TTF price only reaches earnings through the smaller portfolio and spot cargo book. A Hormuz de-escalation — Iran said an Oman transit agreement was nearing completion — reopens Qatari flows and collapses the international spread before it ever shows in a quarter.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the stock has already run 48% off its 200-day low and the supply shock has been live since March, so it is priced. Two things argue otherwise: LNG has lagged XLE by 4.9% over the past month while leading it by 5.6% over three, meaning it consolidated through the very week crude spiked, and it sits 8.3% below its 200-day high while VLO, PSX, OKE and TRGP are all within 4.5% of theirs — this is the least extended large-cap energy name on the fetched screen, not the most.

catalyst.action: do not buy ahead of the print. Let 2026-09-10 clear, then accumulate in thirds: first below 240, second below 228, third below 215. Two to three quarters to build; no need to rush.

thesis: Adobe has compounded EPS through the whole AI panic — the fetched quarterly record is 5.31, 5.50, 6.06, 5.96 for $22.83 trailing non-GAAP, with the company guiding Q3 to 6.05-6.10 and consensus revenue near $6.7B on roughly 12% growth — while the multiple collapsed to about 10.4x forward earnings of ~$25, a level that prices structural decline rather than 12% growth. AI-first ARR more than tripled past $500M, meaning Adobe is currently monetising the technology the de-rating says will kill it, and a $25B repurchase authorisation retires shares into the discount.
key_risk: The bear case is not that Adobe misses a quarter, it is that generative image and video models make per-seat Creative Cloud licensing obsolete over five years, in which case earnings stop compounding and a 10x multiple turns out to have been correct rather than cheap. Concrete invalidation: Digital Media net-new ARR falls year-over-year for two consecutive quarters, or Creative Cloud subscription revenue growth drops below 5%. That is the seat erosion the thesis denies, showing up in the numbers rather than in the multiple.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that cheap software has stayed cheap all year and the positioning evidence is genuinely mixed, not supportive: the fetched analyst trend has bullish share falling 3.1 points with revision direction reading deteriorating, and insiders sold $18.9M against $1.9M bought over six months. What answers it is the composition of that single purchase — a director buying 10,000 shares on the open market at 194.51 on 2026-06-25, near the lows, is the one insider transaction type with predictive content, and it is a buy.

thesis: Dollar General has beaten consensus EPS in all four of its last four reported quarters on the fetched record — 1.28 vs 0.97, 1.93 vs 1.70, 2.00 vs 1.94 and most recently 2.23 vs 2.07 — and still closed 127.87 on 2026-09-08 after a 4.0% session, sitting right on its 200-day average of 126.22 with the 20-day (124.64) and 50-day (122.98) rising underneath it. key_risk: The gasoline channel cuts both ways and has burned this thesis before: higher fuel raises DG's own distribution costs and takes dollars out of the basket at the same time as it drives traffic through the door, so traffic can rise while comparable sales and gross margin fall. instrument: Kalshi — Fed hikes 25bps at the 2026-10-28 FOMC meeting

catalyst.event: FOMC decision 2026-10-28, with the September CPI release on 2026-10-14 landing two weeks ahead of it — the first print that will carry the gasoline pass-through from a crude move that happened almost entirely in September. Resolution source is the FOMC target-range announcement; contract closes 2026-10-28T13:59 ET.
catalyst.action: RE-AFFIRMS the level published 2026-09-02 at 28 — it is unchanged and still on the ask. Buy 26-30, size as a lottery ticket, and be willing to hold to resolution rather than chase.

thesis: The market has quietly repriced the Fed from easing to tightening and has not yet extended that to a second move. The fetched Kalshi ladder puts a 25bp HIKE on 2026-09-16 at 54 cents against 44 for a hold and 1 cent for a cut, and the bond market agrees — the 2-year at 4.37% sits 74bp above an effective fed funds rate of 3.63%. But October is still priced 68/69 for a hold and only 27/28 for a hike, which is a one-and-done. My estimate is 40% against the market's 28%: a committee that hikes on 16 September will read the 14 October CPI print with WTI at 94.24 and Brent near 99 after a ~10% week, on top of an August print the market already prices as near-certain to be above 2.9% year-over-year.
key_risk: This is a conviction 2 and the thinness is the point: the entire edge is one inference about committee behaviour, drawn from market pricing and the rates curve, with no FOMC minutes, no dot plot and no Fed speaker commentary read this session. Central banks also routinely look through an energy supply shock to core inflation, which is the standard doctrine and would leave October a hold. Sized at 1% as a lottery ticket for exactly that reason.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that back-to-back hikes are rare for a data-dependent committee late in a cycle, and that with unemployment at 4.1% a second move risks the labour market for an oil price the Fed cannot influence. That is the better argument and it is why the estimate is 40% rather than 60% — the claim is not that October is likely, it is that 28 cents is too cheap for it, an 8-point edge over the 28% break-even the entry price itself implies.

evidence.detail: Fetched Kalshi ladder 2026-09-09: KXFEDDECISION-26SEP H25 bid 54/ask 55 (OI 4.04M), H0 44/46 (OI 10.33M), C25 0/1 (OI 6.52M); KXFEDDECISION-26OCT H0 68/69, H25 27/28 (OI 35.1K), C25 3/4. Corroborated by FRED: 2-year 4.37% (2026-09-04) against effective fed funds 3.63% (2026-09-07), a 74bp gap, with the 10-year at 4.78% and the 10y-2y curve at +0.41.
